title: Neural reconstruction supports rewritable two-dimensional DNA data storage
summary: A molecular storage demonstration encoded image data in synthetic DNA sequence and rewritable metadata in DNA-backbone nicks. GatedConvolution and EdgeConnect neural inpainting helped reconstruct images after sequencing/readout errors, alongside non-neural detection, smoothing and enhancement steps. Experiments reconstructed an image library and erased/re-wrote metadata, demonstrating a bounded physical storage capability. Image inpainting produces approximate visual reconstructions and does not establish lossless recovery of arbitrary data or universal data-erasure guarantees.
ai_technology: GatedConvolution and EdgeConnect neural image inpainting
organization: University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign; Dorna Robotics

evidence.tested: Synthetic-DNA storage/readout of images, computational reconstruction using neural inpainting and other processing, and experimental metadata erasure/rewriting. Reconstruction was assessed in the demonstrated image-storage setting.
evidence.unknown: Visual image reconstruction is approximate and setting-dependent. The main article was reviewed; detailed supplementary algorithm protocols and general reliability/privacy guarantees were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: Existing neural inpainting models replace masked, corrupted image pixels during decoding of experimentally read molecular data; they are components of a broader experimental storage platform.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher main article abstract, storage/reconstruction Results, named neural-inpainting workflow, main Methods, publication date and author affiliations; supplementary algorithms not reviewed.
